paragraphs.text: Anthropic is giving subscribers on the Claude Pro, Max, Ultra and Team plans one free full reset of their usage limits, covering all models and all limits. The company announced the offer through its ClaudeDevs account on X on November 10, 2026, according to Startup Fortune and CellCog.

The reset has to be used before 2:00 p.m. Pacific time on December 10, 2026, which is 30 days after the announcement. Phemex News, citing PANews, reported the same deadline and described the offer as a one-time reset for paid users.

Anthropic said it had recently fixed a few small issues that used more of users' limits than intended. The company did not describe the issues, say when they began or say how many accounts were affected, according to both Startup Fortune and CellCog. Startup Fortune reported that Anthropic said the issues did not affect every user.

Anthropic also acknowledged that the Fable limit resets it handed out around the launch of Fable 5.2 on November 9 did little for subscribers who had already reached their weekly limit for all models. A Fable reset only restores weekly usage spent on Fable models, CellCog explained, so usage on other models stays counted. The new full reset is meant to cover that gap.

Subscribers can find the reset under Settings and then Usage in Claude on the web, in the Claude desktop app or in the mobile app, where a Reset for free button appears in the limit resets section, according to CellCog. The button is not available inside Claude Code in a terminal or an editor, but because limits are shared across an account, a reset made in the app also applies there.

CellCog listed several conditions. The reset cannot be undone once used. It does not refund extra usage that has already been billed and does not change a usage credit balance. Weekly limits still refill on their usual day and time. Subscribers who downgrade or cancel before using the reset lose it.

Startup Fortune pointed to a Claude Code bug report filed on GitHub on November 9 by a Team plan user on Windows, who said weekly and five-hour limits had been draining much faster since roughly mid-October even though the number of logged tokens had gone down. A colleague on another seat reported the same pattern, and the report linked a second issue describing a similar jump on a Max plan. Startup Fortune noted that these are individual accounts and do not prove a cause.

The reset is a practical fix for people who lost usage, but it leaves the main questions open. Without an account of which bugs were involved and how long they ran, subscribers cannot tell how much usage they lost, and heavy users on the most expensive plans have no way to check whether one reset makes up for it. Usage limits have become one of the most sensitive parts of paid AI plans, and unexplained drains tend to erode trust faster than a single compensation offer can restore it.

The next thing to watch is whether Anthropic publishes details on the fixed issues before the December 10 deadline, and whether usage complaints on GitHub and social media fall off now that the fixes are in place.
